The peripheral assertion about the single-classroom scope is supported by "The participants in this study were one teacher and 33 students at a Chinese university" and "The students in the study were 33 third-year Chinese students, six males and 27 females, majoring in English in the same class". No assertion is contradicted and no hedge is removed (the source itself asserts the limitation), so the claim is verified.

verifications.evidence_quote: the cognitive load imposed by revision after DCF+G was significantly lower than that after ME+GN (p < 0.001, SE = 0.350)
verifications.explanation: The claim's central proposition — that learners reported significantly lower mental effort when processing direct corrections targeting grammatical issues — is stated in the source. Section 5.4 reports: "the cognitive load imposed by revision after DCF+G was significantly lower than that after ME+GN (p < 0.001, SE = 0.350)", and the abstract states "learners’ cognitive load estimates proved significantly lower processing direct corrections targeting grammatical issues." The mental-effort scale (Paas, 1992) is the measure of cognitive load, so "mental effort" and "cognitive load" refer to the same measure. The significance qualifier is supported by the reported p < 0.001. No assertion is contradicted and no peripheral assertion is absent, so the claim is verified.

verifications.claim_text: This case study's single-classroom scope limits generalisability
verifications.evidence_quote: We recognise, of course, that a case study has limited generalisability and reflects the thoughts and practices of individuals in one context.
verifications.explanation: The claim has two propositions: (a) the study is a case study confined to a single classroom (one teacher and 33 students in one class at a Chinese university), and (b) this scope limits generalisability. Both are stated in the source. The central assertion — that the single-classroom scope limits generalisability — is supported by "While focusing on one teacher and 33 students raises issues of generalisability, it is a valuable means of investigating issues of student engagement in considerable depth" and by "We recognise, of course, that a case study has limited generalisability and reflects the thoughts and practices of individuals in one context." The peripheral assertion about the single-classroom scope is supported by "The participants in this study were one teacher and 33 students at a Chinese university" and "The students in the study were 33 third-year Chinese students, six males and 27 females, majoring in English in the same class". No assertion is contradicted and no hedge is removed (the source itself asserts the limitation), so the claim is verified.
